var_label: Average daily PM2.5 concentration from monitors
var_def: The arithmetic mean of PM2.5 measurements for all monitors within the geographic unit. All days during the time span where data is available are included in the dataset. If PM2.5 data is not available for a particular day, then the PM2.5 mean are missing values.

var_label: Standard Deviation of daily PM2.5 concentration from monitors
var_def: Standard deviation of PM2.5 measurements for all monitors within the geographic unit. All days during the time span where data is available are included in the dataset. If PM2.5 data is not available for a particular day, then the PM2.5 standard deviation are missing values. A higher value indictates more variability in the PM2.5 measures used to calculated the mean and median values.

Number of monitors used to calculate daily PM2.5 average and variance measures for the geographic unit. All days during the time span where data is available are included in the dataset. If PM2.5 data is not available for a particular day, then the PM2.5 number of monitors are missing values. A higher number indicates more monitors were used to calculate the PM2.5 metrics.

Total number of collisions, this is the count of all the collisions that occurred in the month.
Total number of collisions that occurred on weekends. Weekends extend from Friday to Sunday.
Total number of people who died because of a collision that occurred in the month.

var_label: Total number of collisions with alcohol involvement
var_def: Total number of collisions where alcohol had involvement, the alcohol use was detected for the responsible driver via a breathalyzer test. The breathalyzer used by police in Mexico indicates alcohol was detected or not and does not indicate the blood alcohol level. It is a screening tool to obtain a legal blood draw test of blood alcohol content.

var_label: Total number of weekend collisions with alcohol involvement
var_def: Total number of collisions where alcohol had involvement on the weekend, the alcohol use was detected for the responsible driver via a breathalyzer test. The breathalyzer used by police in Mexico indicates alcohol was detected or not and does not indicate the blood alcohol level. It is a screening tool to obtain a legal blood draw test of blood alcohol content. Weekends extend from Friday to Sunday.
Total number of people that resulted injured because of a collision.
Total number of fatal collisions, this is the total count where a person died due to a collision.

var_label: Total number of fatal weekend collisions
var_def: Total number of fatal collisions, this is the total count where a person died due to a collision. Weekends extend from Friday to Sunday.

var_label: Total number of collisions with injured person (without deaths)
var_def: Total number of collisions that had at least one injured person excluding collisions in which a death occurred, this variable excludes collisions that had at least one person die.

var_label: Total number of collisions that had at least one injured person
var_def: Total number of collisions that had at least one injured person regardless of whether a death occurred. This variable includes collisions with injuries and deaths, and collisions with injuries but without deaths.

var_label: Total number of weekend collisions with injured person (without deaths)
var_def: Total number of collisions that had at least one injured person excluding collisions in which a death occurred, this variable excludes collisions that had at least one person die. Weekends extend from Friday to Sunday.

var_label: Total number of weekend collisions that had at least one injured person
var_def: Total number of collisions that had at least one injured person regardless of whether a death occurred. This variable includes collisions with injuries and deaths, and collisions with injuries but without deaths. Weekends extend from Friday to Sunday.
Area in km2 of the administrative boundary. This is the total area, including land and water, within L3's boundary.

Measures the average ratio of network distances to straight-line distances. Average of the length of each edge divided by the great circle distances between the nodes of each edge.  Interpretation: For each edge in the network, its circuity is the ratio between the edge length and the straight line distance between its two end points. Varies from 1 to infinity, where streets that are straight lines have circuity of 1, and curved streets have higher circuity. Year of data: September 2017 for L1, January 2018 for L2

Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network. Total number of intersections measures the number of nodes with more than one street emanating from them (thus excluding dead-ends). Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2, 2020 for L3.

Measures the amount of intersections per km2 of area. Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network. Node density of the set of nodes with more than one street emanating from them (thus excluding dead-ends). Higher values means more connected. Interpretation: Varies from 0 to infinity. Cities with higher values have a lot of intersections by unit of area. Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2, 2020 for L3.

Measures the amount of intersections where exactly 3 streets meet per km2 of area. Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network. Node density of the set of nodes with 3 streets emanating from them. Higher values means more connected. Interpretation: Varies from 0 to infinity. Cities with higher values have a lot of intersections with 3 incoming streets by unit of area.Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2

Measures the amount of intersections where exactly 4 streets meet per km2 of area. Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network. Node density of the set of nodes with 4 streets emanating from them. Higher values means more connected. Interpretation: Varies from 0 to infinity. Cities with higher values have a lot of intersections with 4 incoming streets by unit of area.Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2

Measures the total length of streets in meters with four or more lanes per km2 of area. Interpretation: Varies from 0 to infinity. Cities with higher values have more large streets per unit of area; Higher values means more traffic, more obstacles, less walkability. Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2.

Measures the total length of streets in meters per km2 of area. Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network and each street segment connecting two intersections becomes an edge in the network. Street density sums of all links in the undirected representation of the network divided by the area. Interpretation: Varies from 0 to infinity. Cities with higher values have a lot of streets by unit of area. Year of data:  September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2, 2020 for L3.

Measures the average length of streets in the street network. Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network and each street segment connecting two intersections becomes an edge in the network. Interpretation: Small values represent smaller blocks and large values represent larger street segments or blocks. Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2.

Measures the distribution of the number of streets that meet at each intersection of the street network. Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network and each street segment connecting two intersections becomes an edge in the network. Interpretation: Varies from 2 to infinity. Higher values mean on average intersections connect to more intersections. Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2.

Measures the distribution of the number of streets that meet at each intersection of the street network.  Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network and each street segment connecting two intersections becomes an edge in the network. The standard deviation of the number of physical streets (i.e., edges in the undirected representation of the graph) that emanate from each intersection and dead-end. Interpretation: Higher values mean more variability in the number of incoming edges (streets) for each node in the network; the statistical and spatial distributions of number of streets per intersection characterize the type, prevalence, and dispersion of intersection connectedness in the network. Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2.

Total street length considering all types of streets within the areal unit. Each intersection (a point where more than 2 streets meet) becomes a node of the network and each street segment connecting two intersections becomes an edge in the network. Street length sums of all links in the undirected representation of the network. Year of data: September 2017 for L1_AD, January 2018 for L2, 2020 for L3.
An indicator variable for sources of L3 boundary

Measure of the Aerial Tram system supply. The aerial tramway is based on the principle of cableways in sightseeing tours in alpine resorts. The aerial tramway is a type or aerial lift which uses one or two stationary support ropes and a third moving rope to move a cabin through a defined path. For the cities where it does not exist, we assume zero as the value of the city. Interpretation: The total length in km of Aerial Tram. A unit with higher values has a bigger aerial tram system. Country team input: The draft of measures was sent to each country team to check for face validity.  Country teams used their expert knowledge and/or any existing criteria used to suggest any changes to the aerial tram variables at L1 and L2 “subcity”.  Year of data: December 2017

Total urban area (in hectares) divided by number of urban patches. Interpretation: Indicator of urban fragmentation. Larger values reflect a larger size of urban development; low values reflect scattered, small development.

Weighted average of urban patch size (in hectares). This value is weighted by the area of each patch. By weighting by patch size, larger urban patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric. Researchers could decide at their own discretion on using this weighted index or the corresponding unweighted one. Interpretation: Indicator of fragmentation. Larger values reflect a larger size of urban development; low values reflect scattered, small development.

Total perimeter of all patches multiplied by the corresponding area weight, and divided by the total area of the geographic unit. This is the area-weighted version of edge density. By weighting by patch size, larger urban patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric. Researchers could decide at their own discretion on using this weighted index or the corresponding unweighted one. Interpretation: Indicator of fragmentation and shape complexity. A higher value indicates, for the same total area of urban patches: (1) there are likely to be more smaller patches versus fewer larger patches, and (2) on average, patches have a more complex shape.

Mean distance (in meters) to the nearest urban patch within the geographic boundary. This value is weighted by the area of each patch. Interpretation: Indicator of isolation among patches of a similar class, a higher value indicates higher level of isolation. By weighting by patch size, larger urban patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric.

Shape index is a ratio of the actual perimeter of a patch to the minimum perimeter possible for a maximally compact patch with the same size. The area-weighted mean shape index is the weighted average of the shape index for each patch within the geographic boundary. This index is weighted by the area of each patch. Interpretation: Shape index ranges from 1 to infinity, with 1 being the index for a patch that is maximally compact. A lower value indicates higher levels of compactness of each individual patch. By weighting by patch size, larger urban patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric.

Measure of overall levels of Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) supply. For cities where there is no BRT system we assign zero as the value of the geographic level. The BRT is a bus-based public transport system designed to improve upon the capacity and reliability of a conventional bus system. A BRT system includes roadways specially designated as corridors for buses and stations for boarding. BRT aims to combine the capacity and speed of a metro and the flexibility and lower cost of a bus system. The total length in km of BRT in the geographic unit. A unit with higher values have a bigger BRT system. Year of data: September 2017. Country team input: The draft of measures was sent to each country team to check for face validity.  Country teams used their expert knowledge and/or any existing criteria used to suggest any changes to the BRT variables at L1 and L_2 “subcity”.

One-way Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) fare in USD. The BRT price trip standard in USD.  The BRT is a bus-based public transport system designed to improve upon the capacity and reliability of a conventional bus system. A BRT system includes roadways specially designated as corridors for buses and stations for boarding. BRT aims to combine the capacity and speed of a metro and the flexibility and lower cost of a bus system. A unit with a higher travel price indicates a higher cost for the user per trip. Year of data: September 2017

Measure of bicycle lane system supply.  Bicycle facilities: public infrastructure and other areas aimed at the exclusive or shared use of bicycles. This can be an exclusive lane of a public road or an independent way where bicycles can transit. Interpretation: The total length in km of bicycle lane. A unit with higher values has more and larger bicycle lanes. Country team input: The draft of measures was sent to each country team to check for face validity.  Country teams used their expert knowledge and/or any existing criteria used to suggest any changes to the bicycle lanes variables at L and L2 “subcity”. In a preliminary audit, we modified the values according to the information of the experts in the countries and the information collected from OpenStreetMap. For each city with a value different from zero or missing, we take the highest value between the value from the official source and OpenStreetMap. Year of data: December 2017

Foundation year for cities at Level 1 (Applicable only to L1AD and L1UX units). Interpretation: Colonial foundation of the city. Earliest date of colonial settlement is used as foundation year when official date was not available or when discrepancies were found between data sources. City foundation years range from 1502 to 1992.

Binary indicator that distinguishes between coastal (with a value of 1) and inland geographies (with a value of 0). Coastal geographies are those with parts of their boundaries within 1 km from the closest coastline, whereas inland regions represent the rest. Interpretation: Coastal regions should be treated differently as they are more influenced by oceans.

var_label: Coefficient of variation of the urban patch size
var_def: The standard deviation of the patch size within the geographic boundary, divided by the mean patch size within the geographic boundary. Interpretation: A higher value indicates a higher level of variation of patch sizes; a lower value indicates a more even distribution of patch sizes

Major climate zone in a geography, indicating its seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns. Interpretation: Representative climate patterns of seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns in a geography. These patterns control for background difference in climate (precipitation and temperature) and biophysical environment (e.g., availability of greenspace and blue space).

Measure level of demand of the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system.  The BRT is a bus-based public transport system designed to improve upon the capacity and reliability of a conventional bus system. A BRT system includes roadways specially designated as corridors for buses and stations for boarding. BRT aims to combine the capacity and speed of a metro and the flexibility and lower cost of a bus system. Interpretation: It is calculated as the ratio between number of users of BRT and total population (applicable only to L1). A unit with higher BRT demand values indicates a system with higher level of demand. Year of data: September 2017.

Total perimeter of all urban patches, divided by the total area of the geographic unit measured in meters per hectare. Interpretation: Indicator of fragmentation and shape complexity. A higher value indicates, for the same total area of urban patches: (1) on average, there are likely to be more smaller patches, versus fewer larger patches, and (2) on average, patches have more complex shapes.

The sum of squares of urban patch size, divided by the total area of the geographic unit in hectare. Interpretation: Indicator of fragmentation where larger patches have higher weights. Larger values reflect a larger size of urban development; low values reflect scattered, small development.
Average elevation over land area (excluding water) in meters. Large value reflects more hilliness.
Maximum elevation over land area (excluding water) in meters. Large value reflects more hilliness.
Median elevation over land area (excluding water) in meters. Large value reflects more hilliness.
Minimum elevation over land area (excluding water) in meters. Large value reflects more hilliness.
25th percentile of elevation over land area (excluding water) in meters. Large value reflects more hilliness or more variations in hilliness.
75th percentile of elevation over land area (excluding water) in meters. Large value reflects more hilliness or more variations in hilliness.
Standard deviation of elevation over land area (excluding water) in meters. Large value reflects more variation in hilliness.

var_label: Differences between worldpop- and census-based population
var_def: Worldpop estimated population minus census-based population then divided by the census-based population. Interpretation: A larger value shows Worldpop-estimated population is higher than census-based population, and vice versa.

False negative rate is the probability that pixels classified as non-urban according to HSR are classified as urban according to GUF (the dataset used to derive the cross-sectional urban patch metrics). The measure was computed using the 2015 data. The false negative rate varies from 0 to 100. Missing values occurred for units that did not have negatives, false positives, true positives, or true negatives (because of missing data, for example) and which had zeroes in the nominator or denominator when computing the rates. Interpretation: Higher values mean a greater probability that non-urban areas per HSR to be classified as urban per GUF.

False positive rate is defined as probability of overlap between urban HSR pixels with non-urban GUF pixels (the dataset used to derive the cross-sectional urban patch metrics) relative to GUF non-urban. In other words, it is the probability that the pixels classified as urban according to HSR are classified as non-urban according to GUF. The measure was computed using the 2015 data. The false positive rate varies from 0 to 100. Missing values occurred for units that did not have negatives, false positives, true positives, or true negatives (because of missing data, for example) and which had zeroes in the nominator or denominator when computing the rates. Interpretation: Higher values mean greater disagreement between HSR and GUF regarding urban pixels.

Measure the price per gallon. Price per gallon of standard gasoline in USD per lite. Interpretation: Price per gallon of standard gasoline in USD per liter. A unit with higher values indicates a transportation system with higher cost for the users and the drivers. The year of the data is from 2017 and range between March to September. A unit with higher values indicates a transportation system with higher cost for the users and the drivers.

Measure the capacity of payment of a unit of fuel, according to the minimum wage. Interpretation: Price of standard gasoline in USD per liter /minimum wage. A unit with higher values indicates a transportation system with higher cost for the users and the drivers.

A variable indicating whether the L3s in an L1AD on average are correctly georeferenced, i.e., have the correct alignment with other geospatial data. BECGEOFLAGL3 = 0 indicates that L3s in an L1AD overall have correct alignment. BECGEOFLAGL3 = 1 indicates that L3s in an L1AD overall have incorrect alignment and we recommend not using these L3s in the analysis.

Total greenspace area (in hectares) divided by number of greenspace patches. Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Indicator of fragmentation. Larger values reflect a larger size of greenness; low values reflect scattered, small greenness.

Weighted average of urban patch size (in hectares). This value is weighted by the area of each patch. Greenspace patches and total area are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Indicator of fragmentation. Larger values reflect a larger size of greenness; low values reflect scattered, small greenness. By weighting by patch size, larger urban patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric. Researchers could decide at their own discretion on using this weighted index or the corresponding unweighted one.

var_label: Area-weighted Mean Nearest Neighbor Distance of greenspace patches
var_def: Mean distance (in meters) to the nearest greenspace patch within the geographic boundary. This value is weighted by the area of each patch. Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Indicator of isolation among patches of a similar class, a higher value indicates higher level of isolation. By weighting by patch size, larger green patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric.

var_label: Area-weighted mean shape index of greenspace patches
var_def: Shape index is a ratio of the actual perimeter of a patch to the minimum perimeter possible for a maximally compact patch with the same size. The area-weighted mean shape index is the weighted average of the shape index for each patch within the geographic boundary. This index is weighted by the area of each patch. Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Shape index ranges from 1 to infinity, with 1 being the index for a patch that is maximally compact. A lower value indicates higher levels of compactness of each individual patch. By weighting by patch size, larger green patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric.

Clumpy measures the clustering of greenspace patches. Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Indicator of spatial clustering of greenspace patches. A value closer to 1 indicates more spatial aggregation, whereas a value closer to -1 indicates more spatial disaggregation.

Cohesion measures physical connectedness of greenspace patches. Cohesion increases monotonically as the proportion of the landscape occupied by greenspace increases until an asymptote is reached near the percolation threshold (beyond which a giant connected component exists). Cohesion=0 if the landscape only has one greenspace cell. Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution.  Interpretation: Indicator of physical connectedness of greenspace patches. A value closer to 0 indicates less connection and less presence of greenspace patches. The value is sensitive to and increases with clumpy of greenspace patches, before the percolation threshold when a giant connected component forms (e.g., a green belt along the city perimeter). Beyond the percolation threshold, cohesion is insensitive to patch configuration.

Total edge of all greenspace patches, divided by the total are of the geographic unit (meters per hectare). Edge is the patch boundary separating greenspace from non-greenspace and does not include the boundary on the landscape boarder. Greenspace patches and total area are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Indicator of fragmentation and shape complexity. A higher value indicates, for the same total area of green patches: (1) on average, there are likely to be more smaller patches, versus fewer larger patches, and (2) on average, patches have more complex shapes.

var_label: Mean Nearest Neighbor Distance of greenspace patches
var_def: Mean distance (in meters) to the nearest greenspace patch within the geographic boundary. Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution.  Interpretation: Indicator of isolation among patches of a similar class, a higher value indicates higher level of isolation. By weighting by patch size, larger green patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric.

var_label: Mean shape index of greenspace patches
var_def: Shape index is a ratio of the actual perimeter of a patch to the minimum perimeter possible for a maximally compact patch with the same size. Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Shape index ranges from 1 to infinity, with 1 being the index for a patch that is maximally compact. A lower value indicates higher levels of compactness of each individual patch. By weighting by patch size, larger urban patches have a higher influence in this weighted-average metric.

Number of contiguous areas of greenspace (greenspace patches hereafter). Greenspace patches are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution.  Interpretation: Higher number of patches reflects fragmentation of green spaces.

Total greenspace area divided by the land area of the geographic unit, and multiplied by 100. Greenspace area and land area  are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX and L3 using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Large value indicates a higher level of greeness of the geographic unit.

var_label: Land area for calculating percentage of greenspace
var_def: Land area in hectares for calculating percentage of greenspace (denominator)

Number of greenspace patches divided by the total area of the geographic unit (number of patches/hectare). Greenspace patches and total area are net of water bodies and exclude limited no observation areas in remote sensing images (due to cloud and shadow). This variable is calculated for L1UX using a 2017 greenspace map at 10 m resolution. Due to the large size of L1AD and L2, this variable is calculated using the same greenspace map resampled to 30 m resolution. Interpretation: Higher patch density reflects fragmentation of green spaces.

The flag is used to mark records where the true positive rate – or the extent of overlap between urban HSR and urban GUF pixels at L1AD in 2015 – is less than 50%. If the true positive rate is < 50%, the flag takes on ‘1’, otherwise it is set to ‘0’.  The flag was computed for 2015 and is available for L1AD, L1UX, and L2.

var_label: Flag for % increase in urban area between 1985 and 2015
var_def: Flag for the percentage increase in urban area between 1985 and 2015. If percentage increase in urban area between 1985-2015 is greater than 149%, the flag is set as ‘1’; ‘0’ otherwise. Interpretation: ‘1’ means that a unit’s urbanized area saw an increase of greater than 149% -- or increased by at least 2.5 times -- by 2015 compared to 1985.

var_label: Maximum of annual maximum NDVI (water excluded)
var_def: Annual maximum Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) in an area. NDVI is an indicator of vegetation ‘greenness’. NDVI ranges from -1 to 1, with higher values indicating more vegetated areas that are also greener. Interpretation: Maximum of the annual maximum NDVI values in effective urbanized area (excluding water and vegetation) with bias-corrections for cloud, heavy aerosols, and shadows. Large value reflects higher prevalence of vegetation, particularly greener vegetation.

var_label: Median of annual maximum NDVI (water excluded)
var_def: Annual median Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) in an area. NDVI is an indicator of vegetation ‘greenness’. NDVI ranges from -1 to 1, with higher values indicating more vegetated areas that are also greener. Interpretation: Median of the annual maximum NDVI values in effective urbanized area (excluding water and vegetation) with bias-corrections for cloud, heavy aerosols, and shadows. Large value reflects higher prevalence of vegetation, particularly greener vegetation.
Value of minimum wage per country in USD. Interpretation: USD at 2017 September

Measures distance to the center of Level 1 units (in km). (Applicable only to Level 2 and Level 3 units). Interpretation: Measures the distance between each L2 and L3 unit’s centroid to L1 city center. A higher value indicates longer distance to the city center.

var_label: Number of Bus Rapid Transit users
var_def: Measure of the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system demand (users per day). The BRT is a bus-based public transport system designed to improve upon the capacity and reliability of a conventional bus system. A BRT system includes roadways specially designated as corridors for buses and stations for boarding. BRT aims to combine the capacity and speed of a metro and the flexibility and lower cost of a bus system. Interpretation: The number of BRT users (applicable only to L1). A unit with higher values indicate that the BRT system transport more users. Year of data: September 2017
Number of contiguous areas of urban development. Interpretation: Higher number of patches reflects fragmentation of urban expansion.

Measure the open street or ciclovías system supply. The  Ciclovías Recreativas in Latin America, Open Streets in North America are programs where streets are open temporarily exclusively for people so they can enjoy safe, free space in their city for cycling, skating, walking, jogging or other activities. Interpretation: The total length in km of streets that are used for the Open Streets or Ciclovía program for recreational purposes (applicable only to L1). A unit with higher values has a bigger open street system. Year of data: December 2017

var_label: Payment capacity of Bus Rapid Transit
var_def: Measues the capacity of payment of a city in the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT), according to the minimum wage (applicable only to L1). The BRT is a bus-based public transport system designed to improve upon the capacity and reliability of a conventional bus system. A BRT system includes roadways specially designated as corridors for buses and stations for boarding. BRT aims to combine the capacity and speed of a metro and the flexibility and lower cost of a bus system. The year of the minimum wage is from September of 2017 in USD. A unit with higher values indicates more expensive systems according to the minimum wage of each country.

Measures the capacity of payment of a city in the Subway, according to the minimum wage (applicable only to L1). The year of the minimum wage is from September of 2017 in USD. Interpretation: It is calculated as the ratio between price trip of subway*10 and minimum wage. A unit with higher values indicates more expensive systems according to the minimum wage of each country.

var_label: % increase in urban area between 1985 and 2015
var_def: A percentage increase in total urban area in 2015 compared to 1985. This is calculated as ((total urban area in 2015- total urban area in 1985)/total urban area in 1985)*100. Interpretation: Higher values mean a more expansive urban growth.

var_label: Percent area covered by seasonal water bodies
var_def: Percentage of area covered by seasonal water bodies (present only in some months in a year) of a geographic unit in a year. Interpretation: higher percentages indicate a stronger presence of water bodies.

Per capita carbon (CO2) footprint of a geography. Interpretation: total and per capita carbon emission (carbon footprint) in a geography based on national or subnational carbon footprint, the geography’s population, purchasing power and expenditure patterns. Higher values indicate greater carbon emissions, which may indicate more emissions of co-pollutants (e.g. NOx, SOx) and anthropogenic heat. To get per capita carbon footprint, we first derived gridded population counts by dividing GGMCF’s total carbon footprint by its per capita carbon footprint. We then calculated total population in a geography using area-weighted sum. We finally calculated a geography’s capita carbon footprint by dividing the geography’s total carbon footprint by its total population.

Gini coefficient of population in all urban patches inside the geographic boundary. Measures the evenness of the distribution of population in units of 100m x 100m grid cells. Ranges from 0 (uniform population) to 1 (highly concentrated population). Population is adjusted for United Nations' country-level population projections. Interpretation: Measures how evenly distributed is the population over the urban area. A higher value indicates an uneven distribution. Using adjusted and unadjusted population will generate the same values.
Population per square kilometer in all the urban patches or administrative area inside the geographic boundary. Interpretation: A higher value indicates a denser urban development pattern.

Interpretation: A binary variable indicating 1 if an Aerial tram system exists in the city, 0 in the other case.  Year of data: December 2017

A unit with higher values of supply of bicycle lanes indicates the presence of a system with greater capacity for attention to the population. Year of data: December 2017.

A unit with higher values of supply of BRT indicates the presence of a system with greater capacity for attention to the population. Year of data: September 2017.

True negative rate is defined as probability that non-urban HSR pixels are classified as non-urban in GUF (the dataset used to derive the cross-sectional urban patch metrics). Missing values occurred for units that did not have negatives, false positives, true positives, or true negatives (because of missing data, for example) and which had zeroes in the nominator or denominator when computing the rates. Interpretation: Higher values mean greater agreement between HSR and GUF regarding non-urban pixels.

True positive rate is defined as probability of overlap between urban HSR and urban GUF pixels (the dataset used to derive the cross-sectional urban patch metrics) relative to GUF urban. In other words, it is the probability that the pixels classified as urban according to HSR are also classified as urban according to GUF. The measure was computed using the 2015 data. Interpretation: Higher values mean greater agreement between HSR and GUF regarding urban pixels.

var_def: Administrative level of the GDP estimate assigned to each SALID1. For L1ADs which incorporate multiple subnational administrative units, levels of all administrative units included in the GDP estimate are concatenated. For example, an L1AD which overlapped both a department and a federal district would have a value of “Department / Federal District.”

Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita (purchasing power parity in constant 2011 international US Dollars). Subnational GDP estimates are based on an extensive econometric analysis by Genaioli and colleagues in 2013. GDP per capita (purchasing power parity in constant 2011 international USD) was estimated globally using complete data available at the smallest administrative unit possible. Within Latin American countries, this subnational level was generally the first-level administrative unit (departments/states/etc.) in addition to federal districts in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, and Nicaragua. The exception is Costa Rica, which has one national GDP estimate and no estimates at the subnational level.

The Gini Index is a widely used summary measure of economic inequality that describes the distribution of wealth or income in a population. The final index calculated ranges from 0 to 1 with 0 expressing perfect equality and 1 expressing perfect inequality. 
Some features of the Gini Index as a measure of inequality are: 1)Population independence: The Gini Index does not depend on the size of the population. However, age structure and population mobility may play a role (people generally have low income when they are younger vs. when they are older); 2) Scale independence: The Gini Index does not depend on the size of the economy. However, it is important to keep in mind that small populations or less diverse economies tend to have small Gini Indices; 3) Transfer principle: if income is transferred from a rich person to a poor person the resulting distribution is more equal. The Gini index was calculated based on per capita household income deciles using disaggregated data on monetary income from salaries, rents, capital, transfers, and other from country household surveys. Data were harmonized across surveys to ensure internal consistency and for comparison between countries and cities, including adjusting per capita incomes for purchasing power parity using 2005 as the reference year and the consumer price index of a given survey year. The primary estimates were completed by the Division of Social Development of CEPAL and verified by the Global Urban Observatory of the UN Habitat.

A summary measure of economic inequality in terms of the distribution of per capita household income in the defined geographic area. The Gini Index is a widely used summary measure of economic inequality that describes distribution of wealth or income in a population. The Gini Index is based on the Lorenz curve, which plots the cumulative percentage of households (from the poorest to the richest) on the horizontal axis against the cumulative percentage of the income or consumption variable on the vertical axis. The Gini Index is calculated as twice the area between the Lorenz curve and the diagonal line crossing the intersection between the horizontal and vertical axes. The final index calculated ranges from 0 to 1 with 0 expressing perfect equality and 1 expressing perfect inequality. Some features of the Gini Index as a measure of inequality are:  
• Population independence: The Gini Index does not depend on the size of the population. However, age structure and population mobility may play a role (people generally have low income when they are younger vs. when they are older) 
• Scale independence: The Gini Index does not depend on the size of the economy. However, it is important to keep in mind that small populations or less diverse economies tend to have small Gini Indi-ces. 
• Transfer principle: if income is transferred from a rich person to a poor person the resulting distribution is more equal.

Captures factors related to poverty and general living conditions. This score includes three variables: (1) the percentage of household with piped water inside the dwelling as a marker of living conditions; (2) the percentage of households with overcrowding (defined as more than 3 people per room, excluding kitchen and bathroom); and (3) the percentage of population aged 15-17 attending school. The latter variable is included because low school attendance among adolescents has been linked to poverty and early participation in the labor market, as well as exclusion from productive systems.  The score was created by summing the Z-scores for each component variable. Z-scores were created based on the distributions of all cities (L1AD) or all sub-cities (L2). For the construction of the score, we reverse coded the overcrowding indicator so higher score values signify better living conditions and lower poverty levels.

Refers to services that cities provide to dwellings. This score includes two variables: (1) the percentage of households with access to water source from a municipal public or private water network, and (2) the percentage of households with sewage system connected to a municipal public or private sewage network. The score was created by summing the Z-scores for each variable. Z-scores were created based on the distributions of all cities (L1AD) or all sub-cities (L2). Higher score values signify better service provision in cities.

Refers to educational achievement in the overall population. We used aggregated data from individual level of education to retrieve (1) the percentage of population age 25 or above that has completed high school level or above, and (2) the percentage of population age 25 or above that completed university level or above. The score was created by summing the Z-scores for each variable. Z-scores were created based on the distributions of all cities (L1AD) or all sub-cities (L2). Higher score values signify better educational achievement in the population.

This index aims to summarize the domains of education, water acces, sanitation and overcrowding. For its construction, one measure from each of the four domains of education (proportion of the population aged 25 or older who completed primary education or above), water access (proportion of households with piped water access inside the dwelling), sanitation (proportion of households connected to a public sewage network), and overcrowding (proportion of households with more than 3 people per room) was selected. Each measure was transformed into a Z-score using the mean and standard deviation from the census data. Overcrowding was reverse coded such that the direction of all measures indicate a better social environment. The four measures were summed then divided by 4 assuming equal weights for all four measures.  This index was developed using data for cities (L1AD), the same method was applied to create the index at sub-city (L2) level. The higher the index the best social environment.

Survey results are presented in three categories: employed, unemployed, or inactive. Employed refers to those who are working for payment, whether for money, products, merchandise, benefits, and/or other remuneration for at least 1 hour during a reference time period (usually a specific week). Unemployed refers to those who are not currently employed, but that are actively seeking employment during a certain time period (usually a month reference period) and are considered part of the labor force. Inactive refers to those who are not employed or unemployed and generally consists of retirees, students, volunteers, and those engaged in personal household labor activities.

var_def: Prevalence estimate of meeting WHO exercise guidelines through global physical activity in adults aged 18 and older. Global physical activity includes physical activity from transportation or leisure time activities.

Prevalence estimate for current smoker amonst adults aged 18 and older. Current smokers are smokers of cigarettes or tobacco products. If a tobacco use question is available, then it is used to create this variable (this follows WHO definitions). If it is absent but a cigarette use question is available, the cigarette use question is used. For CO-ENSIN2010, GT-DHS2015, NI-CAMID2003 and PE-ENDES2016 where lifetime smoking is not available, this uses the version of current smoking available for that survey. NI-CAMDI2003 is current tobacco use > 100 and CO-ENSIN2010, GT-DHS2015, and PE-ENDES2016 are current cigarette use any amount. Recommendations: For most analyses, the combined version of cigarette and tobacco use (SVYSMKHX and SVYSMKCUR) can be used. Caution should be taken in the interpretation given the differences in how tobacco use is collected.

This measure was adapted from the Gender Inequality Index developed by the United Nations Development Fund (UNDP), which uses country-level data to characterize three dimensions: health (maternal mortality and adolescent birth rates), empowerment (education and government), and the labor market (labor force participation). This index is a measure of the loss in potential human development due to inequality between women and men in these three dimensions. It ranges from 0, indicating a context where women and men fare equally, to 1, indicating a context in which one gender fares poorly compared to the other in all measured dimensions. For SALURBAL cities, we adapted the index to capture gender-based disadvantage and created 2 versions, one including the three dimensions and the other one including only two dimensions: empowerment and the labor market. This is the verion using all three dimentions. It was constructed using city level data from vital registrations and population projections, census: % female and male labor force participation, % female and male population 25+ with at least high school education, and the % women and men in mayoral positions in the government for the period of 2010-2015 obtained from different sources for each country.  To construct the index, we followed the formulas described by UNDP.

This is the verion using two dimentions. To construct the index, we followed the formulas described by UNDP.

var_label: Labor Force Women’s Achievement (or women's achievement score 1)
var_def: The variable captures factors related to employment and marriage. This score includes two variables: 1) % of women in the labor force, 2) % women 15-17 married among the female 15-17 population.  For the construction of the score, we reverse coded the marriage indicator so higher score values signify higher achievements. A higher value indicates higher achievement among women. The variable uses census measures: The labor force participation rate among the female population 15 years or above and the proportion of females aged 15-17 who were married among the total female population ages 15 to 17 (reverse coded). Women's achievement scores were derived from a principle components analysis.

var_label: Education Women’s Achievement   (or women's achievement score 2)
var_def: The variable captures factors related to women’s education. It includes 2 indicators: 1) % women ages 25+ with at least high school education (Proportion of the female population aged 25 or older who completed secondary education or above), 2) % women ages 25+ with at least university education (Proportion of the female population aged 25 or older who completed university education or above). A higher value indicates higher education among women. This version of Education Woman’s Achievement includes all L1ADs where census measures are available and the z-scores are created using the mean and standard deviation of the whole sample. Women's achievement scores were derived from a principle components analysis.

var_label: Health Care Women’s Achievement (or women's achievement score 3)
var_def: The variable refers to health care for women. This score is only available for a limited number of countries (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Mexico). We estimated the prevalence of women ages 25 to 49 with a pap test in the last 3 years and the prevalence of women 50 to 49 with a mammogram in the last 2 years. These measures were used as indicators for health care for women.  A higher value indicates better health care among women. Women's achievement scores were derived from a principle components analysis.

var_label: Labor Force Women’s achievement with health care indictors
var_def: The variable captures factors related to employment, marriage, and health care indicators. This score includes four variables: 1) % of women in the labor force, 2) % women 15-17 married among the female 15-17 population, 3) % women 25 to 49 with a pap test in the last 3 years, and 4) % women 50 to 79 with a mammogram in the last 2 years. For the construction of the score, we reverse coded the marriage indicator so higher score values signify higher achievements. A higher value indicates higher achievement. This score is available in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Mexico. Women's achievement scores were derived from a principle components analysis.

var_label: Education Women’s achievement excluding countries without health care data
var_def: the variable captures factors related to women’s education standardized only to the countries where health care indicators are available. It includes 2 indicators: 1) % women ages 25+ with at least high school education, 2) % women ages 25+ with at least university education. This version uses the same variables as the Woman’s Achievements score 2 (CNSWA2L1AD) with the only difference being that this version creates Z scores for the score components using only the countries with health care data (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Mexico). This variable is created by standardizing education variables to the distribution of the L1ADs with health care measures available. Women's achievement scores were derived from a principle components analysis.

var_label: Women’s empowerment score 1- Labor force participation
var_def: The variable refers to women’s participation in the labor force depicting some aspect of women’s socio-economic position.  Since it includes the relation of female to male in educational attainment and in labor force participation, it is also accounting for gender inequalities in education and labor market that have been described as relevant in low- and middle-income countries.It includes the following indicators: ratio female/ male in population aged 25 and over with high school level or above; ratio female/ male in population aged 25 or above with complete university or above; labor force participation among women; and ratio female/male in labor force participation. Higher score values signify greater participation of women in labor force and greater education of women relative to men. Women's empowerment scores were derived from a principle components analysis.

This variable refers to the level of educational attainment among women and was used as a measure of differences within women. It includes: % female population with at least complete high school among female population aged 25 years or above; and % of female population with complete university or above among female population aged 25 years or above. Higher score values signify greater education achievement among women. Women's empowerment scores were derived from a principle components analysis.
